_doc: Hand-written (no generator). The five-minute video as deep links into the four story pages (ui/index.html; docs/story-contract.md URL scheme: page=configure|running|run|results|learnings, s=<scenario id from ui/data/story/index.json>, k=<step, minutes after 16:00>, q=<1-4>, tf=<transformer index>; defaults omitted, speed defaults to 0.25). docs/demo-script.md lists the same ids, links and clock; the audited numbers, each with its label, file and field, are in presentation/NUMBERS.md. Captions and headlines are TEMPLATES: prose plus {{fact}} placeholders that ui/panels/more.js resolves from the committed JSON with their honesty label (the Engine explorer); {{chip:LABEL:cite}} labels a prose claim; [[...]] is an optional clause, dropped whole until the data it names is built. No caption, headline or title carries a bare digit: a number with no fact is read from the page, never typed here. t0/t1 are the video clock. A refuted expectation is stated as measured, never asserted. Every no-violation claim says 'because of batteries'.

beats.title: The problem
beats.label: REAL
beats.headline: ERCOT sends one number per zone and checks no street transformer, while Base's Houston set point already moves as one block ({{houstonBlock}}).
beats.caption: ERCOT dispatches one number per load zone and does not check feeders {{chip:REAL:ERCOT ADER Governing Document Phase 3.3: identified distribution limits are not enforced when an ADER is awarded or dispatched; one number per ADER}}. Base's own Houston partition already moves as one block: its set point went to {{houstonBlock}} {{chip:REAL:Base blog, aggregated-ders-and-the-capacity-crunch: the table's Set point column, from zero; the fleet realized slightly less}}. Our naive policy is our assumption of one number, no feeder check, all at once at the onset {{chip:ASSUMPTION:Base's real split is not public; never implies Base charges this way today}}. The feeder is an Oncor-suburb stand-in on NREL's synthetic feeder {{chip:REAL:REAL dataset, synthetic feeder: NREL SMART-DS is realistic but not real}}, with a fleet of {{fleetSize}} batteries in a deliberate stress placement {{chip:ASSUMPTION:a cluster placed on purpose on the densest homes plus random homes (data/fleet.json)}}. Street A–D: {{streetHomes}} homes on {{streetTfs}} service transformers. Pick the demo evening and start the sim.

beats.title: Running, honestly
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: No fake progress: the evening already ran in the engine, and the screen shows what it cost ({{msPerStep}} a step).
beats.caption: The Running screen loads the files this scenario plays and shows the engine's measured cost for the run (ui/data/engine.json and the scenario's engine block): OpenDSS solves every minute of the evening, one step in {{msPerStep}}, measured on a shared machine. Nothing is simulated in the browser.

beats.caption: The price falls from {{eveningPeakPrice}} at {{eveningPeakT}} to {{onsetPrice}} at {{onsetT}}, the charge onset. This rule's fuse opens above {{fusePct}} for {{fuseMinutes}} {{chip:ASSUMPTION:the team's round-one rule; A stayed above it one minute short of the rule}}; it operated on {{naiveProtection}} transformers.

beats.label: SIM

beats.caption: Feeder-aware: before sending charge, check each transformer's room and send only what fits. Battery-caused normal-tier events: {{awareBatteryNormal}}; emergency: {{awareBatteryEmergency}}. {{awareVerdict}} What the controller sees: {{controllerView}}.

beats.title: Pieces fail
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: A battery goes silent, an EV plugs in, our controller stalls: still {{faultsBatteryNormal}} battery-caused overloads.
beats.caption: At {{faultCommsT}} the battery at {{faultCommsHome}} goes silent holding a {{faultCommsKW}} command. What it does next is real: it idles in backup-only mode and never discharges to the grid {{chip:REAL:Base engineer, on site, 26 Sep 2026 (verbal)}}. Our timings: stale after {{staleS}}, expired after {{ttlS}} {{chip:ASSUMPTION:COMMS_STALE_S and COMMAND_TTL_S are our timings}}, and {{faultCover}}. At {{faultHotT}} {{faultHotTf}} runs hot ({{evKW}} of new load for {{faultHotMinutes}}). {{faultHotOutcome}} At {{faultStallT}} our controller stalls for {{stallMin}}; every command expires on schedule. Battery-caused normal-tier events: {{faultsBatteryNormal}}; emergency: {{faultsBatteryEmergency}}.

beats.title: Controller crash
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: We kill one of three controller workers mid-charge; another takes its batteries over, and the crashed worker's late commands are refused.
beats.caption: Three controller workers hold leases on groups of transformers. We kill one while it holds a group {{chip:SIM:ui/data/p1/worker_kill.json runtime.kill}}; its batteries run on their last commands until they expire. When the lease runs out, a surviving worker takes the group over at a new epoch {{chip:SIM:runtime.takeover}}, and every late command from the crashed worker is refused as stale {{chip:SIM:summary.rejectedStaleEpoch}}. Read the takeover time, the refused commands and the tracking error from the failures list: no transformer passes its limit because of batteries {{chip:SIM:summary.batteryCausedNormal}}.

beats.title: Hidden attacker
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: A fictional attacker hides a signal in two dozen Cores' charging; the detector reads physics, not command logs, and quarantines them.
beats.caption: A fictional attacker {{chip:ASSUMPTION:a fictional adversary; no real company or person}} takes a shard of Cores and hides a small carrier in their charging. Our detector compares each battery's telemetry with its peers and with its home's own voltage {{chip:SIM:ui/data/p3/covert.json summary}}: read how fast it flags the first unit and the whole shard, the false alarms, and what a simple fixed threshold would have caught, from the quarantine list.

beats.title: Why the grid can't see it
beats.label: DERIVED
beats.headline: A fleet-scale hijack moves ERCOT frequency by a band inside its normal wander: the risk, and the detection, live on the feeder.
beats.caption: The ERCOT context panel shows the real frequency of a different day {{chip:REAL:ERCOT dashboards, 25 Sep 2026 (ui/data/ems/freq-series.json), not the simulated evening}} beside the band a thousand-battery hijack would move it by {{chip:DERIVED:the three-to-seventeen millihertz band, docs/research-report.md; never one value}}. The band sits inside the day's normal wander. ERCOT cannot see it; the feeder can.

beats.title: How many fit
beats.label: SIM
beats.headline: Same feeder, from empty: feeder-aware fits {{capAware}} batteries with {{capAwareOdssCaused}} battery-caused events in OpenDSS; naive runs out long before.
beats.caption: How many batteries fit before the grid is harmed? Feeder-aware fits {{capAware}}, {{capAwareStop}}; OpenDSS measured {{capAwareOdssCaused}} battery-caused events and the cable at {{capAwareOdssHead}} at most. Naive's answer is OpenDSS's, read from the tile {{chip:SIM:ui/data/p2/index.json usefulCapacity.naiveOpenDSS: the largest naive build that holds, and the first that fails}}; the screening count of {{capNaiveScreen}} is refuted: OpenDSS found {{capNaiveOdssCaused}} battery-caused events and the cable at {{capNaiveOdssHead}} there. Voltage is not in this harm test: in the feeder-aware build one home dips just under the floor, to {{capAwareVmin}}.

beats.title: Which transformers to upgrade
beats.label: DERIVED
beats.headline: Every upgrade is priced at Base's own figure against the gross energy value of the batteries it unlocks; more home load does not change the list, because the utility's nameplate rule binds.
beats.caption: Each upgrade is priced at Base's own per-transformer figure {{chip:REAL:PLAN_UPGRADE_USD: Base's figure in its PUCT filing (docket 54224 item 49), not a quote; ui/data/p2/planner.json money.upgradeUSD}}, against each battery's yearly gross energy value, not Base's profit {{chip:DERIVED:PLAN_MEMBER_VALUE_USD_YR: one Core, 2025 LZ_NORTH, planned on public day-ahead prices; planner.json money.memberValueUSDYr}}: read the cost, value and payback on each row. The top four are Streets A–D, over the utility's nameplate rule only because our stress placement put one battery more on each than the rule allows {{chip:ASSUMPTION:the prototype's stress placement (planner.json tfs installed)}}; every home there is already a member, so the verdict is tell the member, don't upgrade {{chip:DERIVED:planner.json rankingByGrowth; the verdict from ui/lib/planner.js decide}}. More home load does not change the list {{chip:ASSUMPTION:growth levels are ours (PLAN_GROWTH_PCTS)}}: the utility's nameplate rule binds, not the physics {{chip:SIM:planner.json rankingByGrowth: the same transformers, in the same order, at every growth level}}.

beats.title: Every evening, same answer
beats.label: DERIVED
beats.headline: On every real evening, naive overloads a transformer and feeder-aware causes none because of batteries; OpenDSS is the referee.
beats.caption: [[Across {{daysCount}} real ERCOT evenings, feeder-aware came out ahead of naive {{daysAwareMoreEvery}} (fleet, gross; on the cheap evening both lose money), {{daysAwareSafe}}; naive overloaded a transformer on {{daysNaiveBroke}} of them. ]]Money is the fleet's gross energy value, not Base's profit. Deterministic code sets every command, no model in the loop; OpenDSS judges every violation.
